summary: Judge A's one gap, that the decision cuts superpolynomial separation claims 'at constant full-RS interval width' without the d<L, KV-certified window the body keeps, was confirmed on 2026-10-21 and reversed by the 2026-10-22 audit: every quantum guarantee the note cites (d/p<C<=L/p, and rate+density>1) needs d<L at constant L, where the DP is polynomial, so outside that window there is no quantum claim for the cut to remove. Judge B flagged the title and the receiver table (5 of 8 controls shown), and both were dropped. The title's 'Actual Receiver' and 'Classical Falsifiers' are accurate names for the executed p=5 receiver and the DP/Babai baselines, and the omitted complex and S={0} controls are discussed under 'Decisive controls', with no conclusion resting on the table. The Cauchy ceiling, the 3/2 tuning bound (451/1395, 19/45 recomputed), the pointwise counterexample and the four Babai certificates hold and match the artifact.

claims.quote: cut claims of a SUPERPOLYNOMIAL quantum-search separation at constant full-RS interval width
claims.finding: A separation needs an efficient quantum algorithm with a guarantee, and every guarantee the note cites lies inside d<L at constant L: Chailloux-Tillich needs d/p<C with C<=L/p for any complex profile, and Sun-Wootters needs rate+density>1, i.e. (1-d/p)+L/p>1, so d<L (and applies only at fixed rates). There the O(N*L*d*p^d) DP is polynomial. Outside d<L the DP costs p^d, but none of the guarantees the note cites applies there (both need d<L), so the cut removes only separation claims the note has no basis for. Carrying 'certified' over from the body would be wording only.

claims.quote: For ANY complex a supported on L elements, Cauchy gives |f(e)|^2<=L/p.
claims.finding: |f(e)|^2<=(sum|a|)^2/p<=L/p, and C<=max|f|^2*sum|f|^2<=L/p, so d/p<C implies rate+density>1. This agrees with the artifact's ceiling 3/5 at p5.

claims.quote: Consequently ANY amplitude tuning changes the real KV codimension cutoff by a factor LESS than3/2 over that simple profile.
claims.finding: Without wraparound, C_uniform=(2L^2+1)/(3pL)>2L/(3p), so (L/p)/C_uniform<3/2. Recomputed 451/1395 at p31,u7 and 19/45 at p5,u1, matching the artifact.

claims.quote: valid probability.722780 and squared fidelity.719020 are BOTH below P_dec=.770203
claims.finding: The artifact's d2 (4,5,4) receiver has worst_fixed_target_conditional_valid_probability 0.7227800 and decoder_success_probability 0.7702026. The one-attempt average .6146>=P_dec^2=.5932, so the counterexample is correctly confined to pointwise use.

claims.quote: Thus the ENTIRE certified constant-width full-RS SEARCH window has a polynomial classical uniform coset sampler
claims.finding: d/p<C<=L/p forces d<L, so for constant L the O(N*L*d*p^d) DP is polynomial in N=p. 'Certified' correctly restricts to the KV sufficient window.

claims.quote: The first four are finite all-syndrome classical certificates, not just selected witnesses.
claims.finding: Babai residuals have GS coordinates in [-1/2,1/2], so the norm bounds hold for every target. The integer bounds 6/5/14/7 are at most u=7/5/15/7, and the p127 bounds 63>31 and 12>11 are correctly reported as inconclusive.

summary: The power-completion and strict zero-avoidance derivations check out: F^(1/r) truncation gives deg(R^r-F)<=(r-1)D-1, and the shifted root R+c raises the degree by at most one. The quadratic-jet character-sum bound also holds. Every live count I checked (344 witnesses, 16 stages, 1934 proposals, 11 moves, 116319 Horner evaluations, and the 108/110, 102->109, 118->124/122 and 29->30 scores) matches the artifact. The tight-degree p5 counterexample holds only for the square coset, which the note does not state; with the nonsquare coset the constant Q=3 is a perfect strict solution at K2. The header's list of open cases leaves out unsolved saved high-rate mixed sources: N31,K16 seed71 (30/31) and the r=3/r=4 mixed controls.

claims.quote: Thus ALL common-coset inputs are solved perfectly whenever K >= (r-1)*ceil(N/r)
claims.finding: Verified: F=lambda^r X^D(...) so F^(1/r)=R+O(1/X), giving deg(F-R^r)<=(r-1)D-1; Q(a_i)-t_i=beta*R(a_i)^r since W vanishes on selected points. Saved global thresholds hold (N16K8: 8<=8; N31K16: 16<=16; N127K77: 64<=77; r3 N63K46: 42<=46; r4 N32K24: 24<=24) and the artifact reports all of these global sources perfect. The N127,K39 global inputs fall below the threshold (64>39) and score 108/127 and 110/127, so the sentence holds only with its condition. Holds in the zero-including mode, which is the section's scope.

claims.quote: Hence K>=b+1 is a uniform sufficient condition for perfect STRICT common-coset completion
claims.step: Strict Nonzero Powers: Constructive Zero Avoidance
claims.finding: c in {0..M} avoids at most M forbidden values -R(a_i) since M<p; (R+c)^r-R^r has degree <=(r-1)D=b. Artifact: all ten strict controls report NATIVE_COMPLETION_WITNESS with full score (the r=4 strict sibling uses K25=b+1).

claims.quote: all25 native polynomials fail perfect strict satisfaction
claims.finding: The coset orientation is not stated, and the claim depends on it. Exhaustive check: with the common square coset (orientation 0, the one tests/test_prime_character_opi.py uses), 0/25 polynomials are perfect. With the common nonsquare coset beta=2, the constant Q=3 gives residuals (3,3,3,2), all nonzero nonsquares, so 1/25 is perfect at K2. The counterexample needs 'square coset' added.

claims.quote: Uniform proposals therefore succeed with probability>=1/3
claims.finding: sum_z chi(z^2+a/beta)=-1 for a!=0 gives an accepted count of (p-chi(beta/beta_i)+Z)/2>=(p-1)/2, and (p-1)/(2p)>=1/3 for every odd p>=3. The degree bookkeeping (h=max(0,2D-K+1), deg(2R0L+L^2)<K) also checks out.

claims.step: Adaptive Root-Value Exchange Is Now Executed
claims.finding: Matches the artifact: K77 mixed 118->124 (seed29) and 118->122 (seed71); K39 102->109 for both seeds; 16 repair stages, 1934 proposals, 11 accepted moves and 116319 Horner evaluations; 344 retained witnesses (=4 r2 configs x4 sources x17 + 2 higher-r configs x4 x9). The pass bound N-initial_score+1 follows from strict improvements.

claims.quote: K39 and general fixed-input/asymptotic solvability remain open
claims.finding: The open-case list names only K39, but other saved high-rate mixed sources are also not perfect in the artifact. N31,K16 mixed seed71 is best 30/31 (r=2, R+rho=16/31+1/2>1, so in the published perfect-search regime). The r=3 N63,K46 mixed sources are 55/63 and 56/63 (R+rho~1.06>1), and the r=4 N32,K24 mixed sources are 28/32 and 27/32. The superseding norm attack covers only N127,K77. The Live Controls paragraph also reports only the r=3/r=4 global controls ('also perfect') and omits these mixed scores.

summary: The two judges agree on every claim: the flat 1/(p-1) Fourier spectrum, the sqrt(5)/6 p5 spread, the whole-ball collision count, the fiber bound M and the pure-distance bound hold. My recomputation confirms epsilon_32=3.19794e-99, TD^2=5.2658e-69, the 42.6x M22 countercontrol, 577/4969/26713 and 343/6859/79507. Both judges flag the headline 'YES', and the gap is confirmed. A non-trivial bound exists only at N127,K39,p=2^61-1 for ell24/32; the bound is already 1 in coherent distance at ell37 (epsilon=2.77e-5, M=2.4e32) and trivially 1 at ell38. The bounded N6 controls have bad-mass bounds 1, 1/3 and 1/7, so ambiguity is not negligible there either.

claims.quote: without randomizing input shifts? YES for the flat-spectrum primes below.
claims.finding: The YES is unqualified by radius or instance. Non-trivial bounds are certified only at one large instance (N127,K39,p=2^61-1, both zero conventions) for ell24 and ell32. Recomputed: ell37 gives epsilon=2.77e-5 but M*epsilon>>1, so the coherent distance bound is 1, and ell38 is the trivial 1 (stated only in Executed Evidence). The bounded N6,K3,ell2 controls have any-radial-weight bad-mass bounds 1 (p7), 1/3 (p19) and 1/7 (p43). The decision does not say that the control fails as the radius approaches capacity, the regime that capacity-DQI targets.

claims.quote: Consequently EVERY nonzero Fourier probability is exactly1/(p-1)
claims.finding: With tau_p=i*sqrt(p), |eta+s*chi*i*sqrt(p)|^2=1+p, so each probability is (p+1)/(p^2-1)=1/(p-1). At p=5 (tau real), (1+sqrt5)^2-(1-sqrt5)^2=4sqrt5 over 24 gives the stated sqrt(5)/6 spread.

claims.quote: It bounds bad source mass for ANY normalized radial weights.
claims.finding: When |S union T|>K, the intersection dimension is j+r-K, and h<=j+r-K-1 is exactly that condition. Spheres have disjoint supports, so the per-sphere bound passes to any radial weights. The formula recomputes to epsilon_32=3.19794e-99.

claims.quote: is well defined, and P(unique herald)>=1-epsilon, trace_distance^2 <= M*epsilon/(1-epsilon+M*epsilon)
claims.step: Coherent Error Is Not Bad Mass
claims.finding: For orthogonal G and B, TD^2=||B||^2/(||G||^2+||B||^2), which increases with ||B||^2<=M*epsilon_actual and with epsilon_actual (it decreases in ||G||^2=1-epsilon_actual), giving the bound. The M22, epsilon 0.01 control gives TD=sqrt(0.22/1.21)=0.426, i.e. 42.6 times epsilon, consistent with 'over40 times'.

claims.quote: Fixed-input source ambiguity upper bound is about3.198e-99
claims.finding: Exact recomputation gives epsilon_32=3.19794e-99, M=1.6466e30, TD^2=5.2658e-69 and TV=7.2566e-35, matching the stated 5.266e-69. The artifact's ell19 bound is exactly 0 and its ell38 bound exactly 1.

claims.quote: They enumerate all577/4969/26713 ball errors and343/6859/79507 coefficient words
claims.finding: 1+6(p-1)+15(p-1)^2 gives 577, 4969 and 26713 for p=7, 19 and 43, and p^3 gives 343, 6859 and 79507. The artifact's actual bad masses (0.288889/0.1/0.046032) match the text.
